name: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd
title: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd - 542830 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: IRCTC FY26 revenue grew 11.6% to Rs 5,475 cr total but PAT only ~6% as CSR and ECL one-offs hit Q4; management reiterates ~30% EBITDA margin aspiration with no capacity or supply-side signal.

summary.headline: IRCTC FY26 revenue from operations rose 11.55% to Rs 5,215 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 27.33% on exceptional items.
summary.overview: FY26 delivered record revenue from operations (Rs 5,215 crore, up 11.55%), total revenue (Rs 5,475 crore, up 11.64%), PBT (Rs 1,875 crore, up 6.72%) and EBITDA (Rs 1,666 crore, up 7.48%). Q4 revenue from operations rose 15.05% YoY to Rs 1,460 crore, but Q4 profit fell to Rs 447 crore from Rs 472 crore, weighed by exceptional items (CSR, ECL provisioning) and a prior-year Rs 48 crore legacy income item not repeating. Management attributed the Q4 margin dip to exceptional items, saying margin would be about 30% excluding them. Catering and tourism grew fast while the internet ticketing segment grew slower. The call was led by the Director (Tourism and Marketing) because the Director (Finance) was unavailable.

segments.name: Catering
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 2,399 crore (+12.89%). Q4 revenue Rs 671 crore (+26.84%), with margin hit by train catering mix, branded catering pilots, ECL and CSR charges; Q4 EBIT margin 6.3% vs 10.4%.

segments.name: Internet ticketing (IRCTC rail ticketing)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 1,536 crore (+7.71%), profit +7.55%. Q4 revenue Rs 390 crore (+4.56%) with EBITDA margin 76%; Q4 EBIT margin 76% vs 85% due to CSR (additional Rs 17 crore), direct costs (~Rs 8 crore) and UPI share (~Rs 8 crore). Claims 89% share of reserved rail tickets.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 890 crore (+19.46%), profit +36.17%. Q4 revenue Rs 304 crore (+10.95%), EBITDA margin 16%; management said margin would be about 18% without CSR (Rs 1.5 crore) and lower margin on two Tejas Express trains.

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 391 crore (+3.17%), profit +21.74%. Q4 revenue Rs 95 crore (+3.26%) with margin improvement attributed to favourable preform (PET) rates and material cost economies.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of about 30%; management declined to commit to mid-30s, saying it aims to maintain 30%.
Forward growth targets by segment: catering around 15%, tourism around 20%, internet ticketing around 7% (convenience fee income targeted at about 10% via unified portal and iPay).
Payment aggregator licence final application deadline is August 2026; management said it expects to meet it and has engaged a tech partner.
Tourism Q1 trend: management said it is 'very hopeful' on domestic tourism, without quantifying.
capex_capacity: Rail Neer: Ambernath expansion tendered from 2 lakh to 3 lakh bottles per day; Danapur from 1 lakh to 2 lakh bottles per day; partner tied up and work ongoing.
Four greenfield Rail Neer plants: land secured at Mysore and Prayagraj; Bhagalpur land deemed unsuitable and re-requested; Ranchi (Barpali) allotment indicated but no formal communication received.
Capital allocation priorities: e-ticketing infrastructure and security, four new Rail Neer plants, expansion of two existing plants, and entry into hotel business.
Asset-light model; cash balance described as strong.
demand_pricing: Q4 tickets booked: 13.39 crore total (AC 6.85 crore, non-AC 6.54 crore); UPI share 51.7%; convenience fee income Rs 247 crore.
Channel partners account for about 28% of ticket bookings; management said the share appears unchanged YoY.
Catering prices are administered by the Ministry of Railways; management declined to comment on a price revision despite gas cost pressure; last hike cited as 2019.
Commercial LPG cylinder shortage in Q4: mitigations included allowing vendors to cook in pantry cars (electric induction), and priority supply tie-ups with IOCL, BPCL and HPCL.
Election special trains contributed Rs 2.38 crore revenue in Q4 and Rs 6.77 crore in FY26.
Dividend payout around 50%; buyback decision rests with DIPAM (Ministry of Finance), and the board has apprised DIPAM.

qa_highlights.question: What exceptional items hit Q4 and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year Rs 48 crore legacy income not repeated; CSR booked Rs 31 crore vs Rs 7 crore last year (incremental ~Rs 24 crore); ECL provision Rs 16 crore vs Rs 8 crore last year. Other expenses were about Rs 109 crore vs a typical Rs 40-50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did catering and internet ticketing EBIT margins fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited exceptional items: catering ECL Rs 16 crore (vs Rs 5 crore), CSR Rs 5 crore (vs Rs 1 crore), legacy item absent (Rs 33 crore last year), and about Rs 3 crore GST impact. For ticketing: CSR +Rs 17 crore, direct costs ~Rs 8 crore, UPI share ~Rs 8 crore. Analyst confirmed CSR and ECL sit in EBIT.

qa_highlights.question: Why was CSR booked in Q4 and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: CSR is 2% of the last three years' profit; projects were sanctioned in Q4. Management called it exceptional and said spreading it monthly would yield about Rs 32-36 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vande Bharat catering model's lower margin change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the licensee fee and turnover both earn margin; the 5% GST on billed turnover, with no ITC credit, is borne by IRCTC on revenue increases.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pending litigation over licence fee for prepaid and postpaid trains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter (CC-60 case) is under litigation and declined to quantify or give a timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rail Neer capacity and partner status?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambernath and Danapur expansions tendered; partner tie-ups in progress; channel partner talks for the 40% supply gap are ongoing but 'not very encouraging' so far.

qa_highlights.question: Did the August Kranti Rajdhani stop at Agra get considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the route is Mathura-Mumbai via Kota and that a request to Indian Railways would be needed; no commitment was made.

risks_watch: Q4 margin compression: exceptional items (CSR, ECL) recurrence, and whether FY27 margins return to about 30%.
Internet ticketing growth slowed to 4.56% in Q4 and about 7.7% in FY26, despite 76% EBITDA margin; convenience fee unchanged for years and under review.
Catering: no fare revision yet; input cost (gas, LPG) pressure on licensees; 5% GST on Vande Bharat billing not recoverable.
Payment aggregator licence by August 2026 and unified portal launch timeline.
Litigation over prepaid/postpaid train licence fee enhancement; unrecognised revenue not quantified.
Rail Neer greenfield plant execution (Bhagalpur land, Ranchi allotment unconfirmed) and partner search.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline records and long-term growth, but defensive on margin compression, attributing it to one-off items. Evasive on dividend/buyback (DIPAM decision), litigation, catering price revision and Q1 tourism trends, saying it could not comment.

growth.why: Management guides segment growth of ~15% catering, ~20% tourism and ~7-10% internet ticketing for FY27 (blended roughly 15% revenue growth), backed by historical trend and Rail Neer plant expansions with no firm timelines, while price revision and capacity timing remain unquantified.
